title.note: Game title, glossary keep; the guide keeps the English title unless the owner gives a Japanese one.

hud.cast.note: Fishing cast = throw the line. 投げる (3rd-grade kanji) is clearer for kids than キャスト.

hud.reel.note: Fishing sense of リールを巻く (reel the line in); same verb as the pass name 自動巻き.

hud.bait_left.note: Item-count form Japanese games use (エサ×12); no plural needed and reads right for 0 and 1. エサ in katakana because 餌 is hard kanji.

hud.backpack.note: Guide and Roblox's ja UI say バックパック. Lint width 12 vs the estimated 10; in pixels 6 kana are about 4.2 x TextSize, close to 'Backpack' in a wide Latin font. If it is cut off, バッグ (Pokemon's word for the bag) fits in 6.

catch.success.note: Guide's tag-bracket pattern keeps the rarity word from needing の/な before the fish name; plain form + ！ for the player's own result. つりあげる in kana (釣 is a junior-high kanji).

catch.escaped.note: 'It got away (from me)'; ～ちゃった carries the light disappointment. In kana because 逃 is a junior-high kanji; no fish word needed.

catch.new_record.note: Japanese writes kg straight after the number with no space (12.4kg). Japan uses the decimal point, so the game's 12.4 reads correctly.

fish.golden_carp.note: 'Golden-colored carp'; species names go in katakana (コイ) as in Japanese field guides and fishing games.

fish.lantern_eel.note: Invented name, translated per glossary: ランタン keeps the glowing-lantern idea and echoes the kept title Lantern Lake. Alternative チョウチンウナギ (like the real チョウチンアンコウ, anglerfish) sounds more like a real species but loses the echo.

rarity.mythic.note: Katakana tier name used in Japanese game UIs (Fortnite's ja rarity set: レア < エピック < レジェンダリー < ミシック), so it reads as the tier above レジェンダリー. 神話 would break the katakana tier set.

shop.rods.note: Fishing rods only; in kana as Animal Crossing writes it (竿 is not a standard school kanji).

pass.auto_reel.note: 'Automatic reeling', built on the button verb 巻く as the glossary asks. オート巻き is the other natural option; オートリール would name the reel device, not the action.

pass.lucky_bait.text: 幸運のエサでレアな魚がつれる確率が2倍に！
pass.lucky_bait.note: Pass name 幸運のエサ shares 運 with the luck stat (friends.boost), per the glossary. 'Doubles your rare fish chance' = 'the chance of catching rare fish becomes 2x', the usual Japanese game phrasing; bold tags kept on the name.

sell.done.text: 魚を{count}匹売って、{coins}コインゲット！
sell.done.note: Counter 匹 must stay in kanji: its kana reading changes with the number (1ぴき, 2ひき, 3びき). Works for count 1. ゲット per the guide instead of 獲得.

ascend.button.note: The guide's standard Japanese game term for a reset-for-bonus prestige; a literal 'ascend' (上昇, 昇天) means climbing or dying, and アセンション is new-age spiritual. If the game later adds a separate Rebirth, Ascend could become 覚醒.

ascend.confirm.text: 転生しますか？最初からやり直しになりますが、レアな魚がつれる確率が{bonus}%アップします。
ascend.confirm.note: Polite form for a confirmation, per the guide. 'now' dropped as filler. 'More often' = 確率が{bonus}%アップ, standard game phrasing. ずっと (permanent) not added because the source does not say it.

weather.storm.text: あらしが来るぞ！レアな魚が食いついてくる！
weather.storm.note: 食いつく is the fishing 'bite' (take the bait). あらし in kana because 嵐 is a junior-high kanji. ぞ gives the excited banner energy.

quest.catch_n.text: 月夜の入り江で魚を{n}匹つる
quest.catch_n.note: Dictionary form, the way Japanese quest lists word objectives. Moonlit Bay -> 月夜の入り江 ('inlet of the moonlit night'); 江 is a junior-high kanji but common in place names, alternative 月夜の湾. 匹 in kanji for the same reason as sell.done.

friends.boost.text: 友達といっしょにつりをすると運+{percent}%
friends.boost.note: Statement with a label-style ending 運+{percent}%, keeping the '+'. 友達 is Roblox's ja word; 運 is the luck stat.

trade.sent.text: {player}さんにトレードを申しこみました
trade.sent.note: 申しこむ ('propose/request') instead of トレードリクエストを送りました, which is 36 wide against the 33 budget. Polite form as a system notice, matching trade.accept; さん after another player's name per the guide.

trade.accept.text: {player}さんがトレードを受け入れました
trade.accept.note: 'your trade' = the request, understood without あなたの. Polite system notice like the guide's trade.request; さん after the other player's name.

codes.redeemed.text: コードを使った！報酬をどうぞ！
codes.redeemed.note: 'Enjoy your reward' as 報酬をどうぞ ('here is your reward'); 楽しんでね would be a calque. Code itself is never in the text.

afk.kicked.text: 放置しすぎたので、つりが止まりました。
afk.kicked.note: 放置 is the guide's word for idling; polite system notice. No mention of leaving the server, as in the source.

settings.back.note: 戻 is a junior-high kanji, but 戻る is the Back button across Roblox's ja UI and Japanese games, so kids know it by sight (the guide's 購入/報酬 reasoning). もどる if the game wants kana.

event.ends.note: Developer: {time} arrives as '2d 4h', which looks foreign in Japanese. A ja build should format it as 2日4時間 (no spaces); the text reads correctly either way.

daily.streak.text: 連続ログイン{day}日目！明日も来て、もっと報酬をもらおう！
daily.streak.note: Streak = 連続ログイン, the Japanese game term for consecutive-day logins; '{day}日目' works from day 1. 'for more' made explicit as more rewards (もっと報酬), per the context; ～しよう call to action per the guide.

tip.night.text: ヒント：夜にしか食いつかない魚もいるよ。
tip.night.note: ヒント： is the usual loading-tip label. 食いつく = fishing 'bite'; friendly ～よ for a kids' tip.

group.join.text: コミュニティに参加して、無料でエサ50個をゲットしよう！
group.join.note: Roblox renamed groups to communities; its ja UI says コミュニティ. 公式 not added since the source just says 'the group'. 50 kept; counter 個 for bait.

leaderboard.biggest.note: 大物 is the Japanese fishing word for a big (heavy) catch; ランキング is the guide's word for a leaderboard and makes the board's purpose clear. Literal 最大の獲物 is stiff and uses a hard kanji.
